Q: Install a GitHub package alongside a CRAN package with the same name A:

You can use devtools::dev_mode() for this. From the man page:

When activated, dev_mode creates a new library for storing installed packages. This new library is automatically created when dev_mode is activated if it does not already exist. This allows you to test development packages in a sandbox, without interfering with the other packages you have installed.

Q: What can be considered as a best practice for manipulating values inside a vector in C++ A:

C++20 is a 6 year old standard at this point, and outside of modules is pretty complete on the Big 3 compilers. C++23 is also essentially complete on the Big 3. There is nothing wrong with pointing out what this could look like in "more modern" C++. Although I subjectively disagree with the vector initialization. It should just be std::vector v{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; for a toy program. Cleaner, and shorter. The AAA mentality almost always leads to harder-to-read code. I get the argument when functions and classes get involved, but this isn't that, and I'd still not like that syntax.

But I'm working under an assumption that this is a learning question asked by someone who should have no issues getting recent versions of tooling, and not a professional who is stuck on something pre-C++20.

Q: Count all occurrences of a string in lots of files with grep A:

If bc is available, another solution is:

grep -chr <string> <directory> | paste -sd+ | bc

Here, grep returns only the count numbers per file - paste chains them into a mathematical addition, and bc solves the calculation.

Q: QueryRecord adds whitespace within CASE WHEN statament A:

A couple years late, but putting this here for the next dev to run into this.

This behaviour follows the SQL Standard. What you are seeing is the result of type coercion in the case expression.

This is a 1992 copy, so a bit hold but this section still applies.
https://www.contrib.andrew.cmu.edu/\~shadow/sql/sql1992.txt

This is the relevant section,

     9.3  Set operation result data types
    
     Function
    
     Specify the Syntax Rules and result data types for <case expres-
     sion>s and <query expression>s having set operators.
    
     Syntax Rules
    
     1) Let DTS be a set of data types specified in an application of
        this Subclause.
    
     2) All of the data types in DTS shall be comparable.
    
     3) Case:
    
        a) If any of the data types in DTS is character string, then
          all data types in DTS shall be character string, and all of
          them shall have the same character repertoire. That charac-
          ter repertoire is the character repertoire of the result. The
          character set of the result is the character set of one of
          the data types in DTS. The specific character set chosen is
          implementation-dependent. The collating sequence and the co-
          ercibility attribute are determined as specified in Table 2,
          "Collating coercibility rules for dyadic operators".
    
          Case:
    
          i) If any of the data types in DTS is variable-length char-
             acter string, then the result data type is variable-length
             character string with maximum length in characters equal
             to the maximum of the lengths in characters and maximum
             lengths in characters of the data types in DTS.
    
         ii) Otherwise, the result data type is fixed-length character
             string with length in characters equal to the maximum of
             the lengths in characters of the data types in DTS.

In your example, you have 2 result types, CHAR(3) for 'cpc' and 'cpm', and CHAR(4) for 'ocpm'. So by the above, it coerces the result to a CHAR(4), which means it will pad 'cpc' and 'cpm' with spaces.

Another example,

CASE
    WHEN col = 'a' THEN '1'
    WHEN col = 'b' THEN '12'
    ELSE = '123'
END

The potential results will be '1 ', '12 ', '123' because it has cast them all to CHAR(3)

So Apache Calcite is correctly following the standard in it's default implementation (RelDataTypeSystemImpl*)of the RelDataTypeSystem interface, and NiFi uses the default implementation in the QueryRecord processor.
*See shouldConvertRaggedUnionTypesToVarying in https://github.com/apache/calcite/blob/main/core/src/main/java/org/apache/calcite/rel/type/RelDataTypeSystemImpl.java

So not really a bug in the framework, just some frustrating nuance that lead me to spend 3 hours learning a fraction of the Apache Calcite code base... so hopefully this response will save the next person the wasted effort.

So we need to either wrap the CASE expression with a TRIM, or cast one of the results to a VARCHAR.

Q: How can I set a breakpoint on a particular file in a Perl program? A:

To debug a Perl script, use the -d switch to invoke the debugger.

perl -d test.pl

Within the debugger you can use b <line no> to set a breakpoint in the current file. Sometimes it is a hassle to set a breakpoint in a file that hasn't been loaded yet or that was loaded a long time ago, so you can also put the line

$DB::single = 1;

anywhere in any Perl program, and the debugger will break immediately after it executes that line. This is also a good way (the only way?) to set a breakpoint in code that will be run at compile time.
